utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-03-70-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we're here this afternoon to conduct the initial appearance before the Tribunal of Mr. Sreten Lukic, and I address myself, first of all, to Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, can you hear the proceedings so far in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: May I now take the appearances. First of all for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thomas Hannis for the Office of the Prosecutor. I'm assisted by Christina Moeller on my left, Carolyn Edgerton on my right, and our case manager, Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. And for the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, my name is Victor Koppe. I've been assigned by the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Koppe. Now, Mr. Lukic, could you stand again, please. I would like to clarify formally your identity. Can you state, for the record, first of all, your full name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 28th of March, 1955.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the address at which you were residing prior to departure to come here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Belgrade. The street of Banjickih Zrtava number 36, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you received an indictment in which you are charged with three other accused, by the names of Pavkovic, Lazarevic, and Djordjevic in a language that you clearly understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you aware that the indictment contains five separate counts or charges against you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Koppe, have you had an opportunity to discuss the terms of the indictment with Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I spoke to Mr. Lukic this morning, but it was a very brief visit so I have not been able to go into great detail in respect of the contents of the indictment. But I...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: But I have spoken briefly with him about the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is he in a position to tender pleas to the various counts on the indictment today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not today. We would like to enter the plea as prescribed in Rule 62, within 30 days from today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you envisage that you will be acting for him at that stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: I assume that is a possibility, but I cannot say at this stage. So far I'm only appearing for him today, but there might be a possibility I will be appearing for him as well within 30 days, but that is, of course, up to Mr. Lukic to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I take it from what you've said so far that there is no point at this stage in going into the detail of the indictment, that that can be dealt with, insofar as it is necessary, when you are in a position, or someone else in is in a position on his behalf to tender an appropriate plea to each of the charges?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: Right, Your Honour. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Hannis, do you see any particular difficulty about continuing the case for the full period of 30 days?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I don't, Your Honour. We have filed a motion to join the co-defendant General Lazarevic with Milutinovic, Ojdanic and Sainovic. We intended that motion to include this defendant and others that may appear later on. But I don't think that is a cause to -- that would bar us giving him the 30 days he is allowed under the Rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So if I appoint an adjourned diet of today's procedure for 29 or 30 days hence or thereabouts, you would have no objection to state to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you have anything else to comment on at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Only, Your Honour, I was aware that, through a media report, that this defendant had some health problems. I know it is not a requirement, but I thought it might be appropriate to address those with him at this time and be sure he is getting all the appropriate treatment he needs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, you can take it, Mr. Koppe, that I will be happy to continue this hearing for the period that you suggest. Is there any other matter that you wish to address me on?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: Not at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you stand again, please. In a moment, I will fix a date when you will appear again at the Tribunal, probably before me, at which stage it will be necessary for you to tender pleas of guilty or not guilty to the various counts against you. That's the only formal matter now that requires to be dealt with this afternoon. However, this is your opportunity to raise with me any matter that you consider it appropriate to raise at this stage on which you think I am in a position to take action. Is there any such matter?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there are no particular issues that I would like to raise. The procedure that concerns my health is under the supervision of a doctor, so there is nothing that I have to object to. I have no proposals to make, because on Monday a cardiologist will come and as of Monday he will be monitoring my health condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic, please again be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: A date for the continued appearance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, what I shall do to bring these proceedings today to a close is to adjourn the initial appearance of Mr. Lukic until Wednesday the 4th of May. There will be a scheduling order issued specifying the time at which that continued appearance will take place. And as I indicated, then, Mr. Lukic, you will require to tender your pleas to the Court. The Court is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: at 4.45 p.m, to be reconvened on Monday, the 4th day of May, 2005. 20 21 22 23 24 25
